Issuers following HAIP accept only a wallet its Wallet Provider has
attested: a Wallet Attestation for the wallet’s instance key, and a Key
Attestation for the keys a credential will be bound to. Your backend
issues them; the app passes the keys and returns its answers. A Key
Attestation request also names the issuance’s instance key, which
attested first, so your backend can give the Key
Attestation that key’s status. A real Wallet Provider attests only
after checking App Attest evidence that it’s talking to your genuine
app.

What a wallet needs before real holders use it.
A credential store of files: one per credential record, in a directory
of the app’s (Application Support, by default). Records are written
with the given file protection — complete by default: readable only
while the device is unlocked — and kept out of backups by default,
since a credential is useless without its holder key, which is in
this device’s Secure Enclave and can’t be restored elsewhere.
